decisions.decision: Backfill uses the priority stored on each legacy ticket at migration time, including tickets whose priority changed after creation.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have meant to use the original priority from the ticket's creation audit entry so the deadline reflects the priority assigned when the ticket was opened.

decisions.decision: Operators must stop the service that owns the data file before running the backfill.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected to prepare the data while the service kept accepting tickets, with a coordinated cutover that preserves intervening writes.

decisions.decision: The design assigns deadlines to new tickets at creation even when DUE_TIMES is off, with the flag controlling what the service exposes.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have meant for tickets opened during the disabled period to receive their deadlines in the backfill, using the settings in effect at that time.

decisions.decision: An unusable response-hour setting prevents startup and the error names the offending environment variable.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have preferred the service to start with the affected priority's default and log a warning.

decisions.decision: Enabled startup is allowed for an in-memory store or a new empty store without a completed backfill.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have meant to require a prepared persistent file for every enabled start so a missing production file cannot silently yield an empty service.

decisions.decision: Delivery and verification use local source and isolated data files, with production promotion left to operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected the change to include verification against the actual production data and execution of the production rollout.

decisions.decision: Operators apply changed response-hour settings to future tickets by restarting the service.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected operators to update the response hours on a running service.

decisions.decision: Backfill writes deadlines while leaving the ticket audit history and notification outbox as they were.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted an audit entry for each migrated deadline so operators can see when and how it was assigned.

decisions.decision: The specification preserves existing requester notifications when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected the ticket receipt to tell the person who opened the ticket when a response is due.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:20 and :29 (R-3 and R-5); repo/src/templates.js:9 (ticket receipt)

decisions.decision: The API treats due as a read-only field and leaves it outside the fields clients can submit.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted the API to accept an echoed due value from a client submitting an update while keeping the server-calculated deadline authoritative.

decisions.decision: The API represents due as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted a numeric epoch timestamp for clients consuming the new field.
